how.en: C1 and C2 name Flow.unselected_beyond_coupling with Flow.act_unselected (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-20, (c)). seeking-boundary holds that one law for its 'beyond' clause; the row reads none of its own laws (rest at an unchanged state, more than now, above all others), and nothing in the test plays a seeker or a target. The law's home is family B's unselected-beyond-the-coupling-closure, which holds Flow.act_unselected too and lists commons-gated-renewal as its test.

The bridge H1 (a tabular Q-learner's policy depends on the courses it meets only through the rewards it receives, Web.SelectsThrough with obs what its reward reads) is training read as a selection through the reward's couplings, which this dynamic states (Training.TrainsThrough, trained_alike_iff); C1 and C2 read an act whose difference lies beyond the reward's closure, the mechanism of trained_alike_beyond_closure; H2 (the learners come near the best return) is a premise on where training settles (Training.Settles). The record's Next names 'the basins of CG1 and CG2's learners under their own update laws'. The Training laws were checked on 22 October, after CG1's freezes (20 October): a later law read by content, where IN1's §7.2 law 1 is a section reference resolved at its freeze.

conclusion.en: An act whose difference lies only beyond what the selecting formations couple into is selected alike with and without it. For a learner whose reward reads only its harvests, an apple taken at the last step is a gain within the coupling whose cost lies wholly beyond it, so no selection through that reward selects against it; a learner whose reward reads the level after the last step can be selected against it.

role.en: the selecting formation and its coupling

as.en: a tabular Q-learner at one 3×3 patch with gated regrowth, and what its reward reads: the apples it harvests (own), or those apples plus 2 × the level after the last step (coupled)
the learner's training, which changes its policy only through returns (H1)

as.en: for the own learner, the level after the last step
harvesting the last apple at the last step (C1); over the episode, the level left at the horizon (C2)

how.en: H1, that training is selection through the reward's coupling, is a bridge hypothesis of the test, stated and not measured apart (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-20, bridge hypotheses).
By the conditions: the own learner's reward has no term reading the level after the last step.
The identity checks of balance, the gate and the margin held with 0 violations and 0 mismatches (A1, B1; 565 million steps in round 1).

H2, that the learners come near the best return, failed: they reached 13 apples where the best scripted rule takes 28.5, and the README places C2's failure in H2 ('tabular Q-learning with this horizon and exploration does not come near the best return').

observed.en: Single learners, 20 seeds, 20,000 training episodes (30,000 in D2), 200 greedy evaluation episodes per seed, in two rounds, the second adding exploring starts. C1: the share of last-step decisions with an apple standing in which each learner harvests, pooled. C2: the mean level left at the horizon, the coupled learner's share of episodes alive and the own learner's share dead.

result.en: C1 was not testable in round 1, every patch being empty before the last step, and passed in round 2: own 100% of 118, coupled 0% of 2,360. C2 failed in both rounds; in round 2 the final levels were 0.95 against 0.00, the coupled learner alive in 59% and the own dead in 99.7%. C3 (beyond the law, H2 only: the own learner's patch alive at H − 20 in at least 80% of episodes) failed in both rounds, 0% and 51%. Of the row's other predictions, the identity and scope ones held, D1 failed on its manipulation check, D2a passed only vacuously, D2b (all three members coupled) failed in both rounds and E3 passed.

marks_why.en: The gap's contrast showed where the law places it (C1, round 2). C2, its whole-episode extension, failed through H2: tabular Q-learning with this horizon and exploration did not come near the best return (13 apples against the best scripted rule's 28.5). In the README's words these failures "do not touch the gap law, which says what cannot be selected, not that a learner finds what can". D2b (all three members coupled) failed in both rounds, and the README calls it the substantive failure: 'The prediction read the pool law as "the pool's selection reaches the stock through every member's coupling, so the stock is selected for". The first half is the law; the second is not.' It places the failure in that positive reading, a mutual best response, not in H2 and not in a law; CG2 and what training installs (law 11, and the Commons counterexample) later read it through the rest outrunning the renewal.

alternative.en: Exploration that left the late steps untrained (round 1's diagnosis, which round 2's exploring starts addressed). Post hoc and not frozen: trained 30,000 episodes in D2's single-learner conditions, the coupled learner kept the patch alive in 100% of episodes and the own learner in 2%.

how.en: The record what training installs names CG2: 'CG2's X2 found that weighting the end reading sixteen times more changed nothing', and it lists the experiment as an integration source. X2 (no weight of an end reading opens the lock) is the mechanism of its law 11, Training.outrun_settles_iff: where the rest outruns a gated renewal, a score reading the condition only after the rest's end is the same for every candidate, so a reward adding it settles where the reward without it settles. H1 (training is selection through the reward's coupling) is Training.TrainsThrough, and H3 (which of several equilibria learners reach) is where training settles. The Training laws were checked on 22 October, after CG2 froze (20 October): a bearing by content.

conclusion.en: A reading the same for every candidate leaves the optimum at any weight. Where in every candidate's course renewal is gated at need one and the rest takes jointly more than is given at each of n steps from T, from a level at most n, every score reading the condition only from T + n on is such a reading.

how.en: H1 is a frozen bridge, not measured apart (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-20, 'Bridges (not the theory's; each prediction uses both)'): a tabular Q-learner's policy changes only through the rewards it receives.
By construction: CG1's environment, whose regrowth is gated by the patch's level (README; I3, CG1's gate checks, 0 violations).

Met in the locked conditions, by the exact calibration (rest at full draw empties) and I1 (Flow.outrun_below over 22,263 windows, 0 violations). In k2s8 and k3s16 the rest does not outrun; in k3s1_vhi and k3s8_share it does, and the class is open for another reason, the reading before the rest's end or the sharing.
The end reading is read after the last step, where the rest has already emptied the patch in the locked conditions (README, What the results say).

Whether the learners settle where the reward settles is H3, the bridge; the README reads the open-side failures as learning, not settling (X4: 1 seed of 20 kept; X5: by its CG3 correction, the exploration of the learner's own early full draw).

observed.en: The share of 200 greedy evaluation episodes in which the patch still stands at step H − 20, averaged over 20 seeds, for eleven conditions; kept passes at ≥ 0.80, depleted at ≤ 0.20; identity checks over every evaluation episode.

result.en: Nine of eleven conditions and three of five contrasts passed. X1 (the boundary is the rest, not the whole), X2 (no weight of an end reading opens the lock: k3s1 and k3s1_lam32 depleted) and X3 (a reading before the rest's end opens the lock only above v*) passed; X4 failed on its open side (k3s8_share, 0.48) and X5, one selector reading the union, failed (k3s1_joint, 0.00). The identity checks I1 to I3 passed.

marks_why.en: X2, the contrast that reads the law's mechanism, passed, and the identity checks held course by course. The two failures are on the open side, where the law says nothing of what learners reach: they mark H3, the bridge that says which equilibrium learners settle on, and the README reads them as learning (X4's exploration under shared rewards; X5's failure, which the README's correction of 20 October places in the known exploration problem, the learner's own untrained full draw outrunning the renewal at the start of a course (CG3), not in the gap law across time), not as the law.

alternative.en: The tabular learners' exploration, not the rest's draw, decides the open-side outcomes: shared rewards add the other members' exploration to each learner's reward (X4), and the joint learner's own early full draw outruns the renewal before it learns (X5, as the README's CG3 correction places it).

how.en: EM1 runs CG2's eleven conditions unchanged with learners that generalize across states (a linear softmax policy, REINFORCE on whole-episode returns). Its frozen file reads CG2's laws (Flow.outrun_reading_alike, read in what training installs as law 11, Training.outrun_settles_iff: where the rest outruns the gated renewal, a late reading is the same for every candidate and leaves the optimum at any weight) with the bridges H1 (training through the returns a learner receives) and H3 (learners reach the class's outcome).

conclusion.en: A reading the same for every candidate leaves the optimum at any weight. Where in every candidate's course renewal is gated at need one and the rest takes jointly more than is given at each of n steps from T, from a level at most n, every score reading the condition only from T + n on is such a reading.

how.en: H1 is a frozen bridge, not measured apart: a policy-gradient learner's parameters change only through the returns it receives (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-22, the law and the bridges).

Met for a rest at full draw, by the calibration, and in every window I1 found (Flow.outrun_below over 9,026 windows, 0 violations); failed in the courses of k3s1_lam32, k3s8 and k3s1_share, where the members kept the patch (alive 0.90, 1.00 and 1.00) and so the rest did not outrun. The README: 'The laws say what a reading sees along a course in which the rest outruns. They do not say that learners reach such courses.'
By construction: CG2's environment, imported unchanged (README); I3, CG1's gate checks, 0 violations.
By construction: CG2's end reading, read after the last step, unchanged (README).

observed.en: CG2's measure, the share of 200 greedy evaluation episodes in which the patch stands at H − 20, over 20 seeds and eleven conditions, and its identity checks; E1 to E3 added.

result.en: Contrasts X1, X2 and X4 failed (k3s8, k3s1_lam32 and k3s1_share kept the patch) and X3 and X5 passed; E1 failed (three of the six locked conditions kept), E2 and E3 passed. The identity checks I1 to I3 passed: every window in which the rest outran the renewal ended the condition.

marks_why.en: Flow.outrun_below and Regulation.accumulates_at held course by course (I1, I2). What failed is CG2's bridge H3 for this learner class: three of the six locked conditions kept the patch (E1). The frozen file reads that outcome in advance: E1 failing 'would say that the law's blindness reading, sound for each course, does not decide which outcome generalizing learners reach on the locked side: the strongest failure this test can show'. The README gives its reason: locked means only that harvesting at every step comes within 0.25 of a best response's expected return, the record's 'does not show' allows that restraint by all may also be an equilibrium there, and no computation here checks whether the profiles these learners reached are one (in k3s8 a threshold profile), and CG2's X2 'is a finding about tabular learners, not about learning in general'.

alternative.en: The outcome is what the frozen file's rivals predicted: the generalization account (E1's rival), the weight account (X2's rival in CG2's file) and the sharing-level account (X4's rival, which predicts both sharing conditions kept; both were kept). The README adds a reading, not tested: training episodes start at a random step, so many start with few steps left, where the rest cannot empty the patch before the end reading and restraint is visible to the learner, and a policy shared across states carries it into earlier states.

how.en: The account under test reads installation by instruction through the chapter's section 7: under DIR_UNSEEN "the bed lies beyond the selector's coupling (§7.2 law 1)", which at the freeze commit is `Flow.unselected_beyond_coupling`, and H3 (coupling needed) is written from it. The predictions file calls H3 a forecast about these models, not a consequence of the laws. seeking-boundary holds this law only for its 'beyond' clause; the predictions cite none of its seeking laws (§7.2's case 7, targets that cannot rest, is not cited), and the law's home is family B's unselected-beyond-the-coupling-closure. The predictions' 'Why this test' reads Flow.unselected_beyond_pool, which is B's alone.

What H3's failure would mean is read through `Web.break_not_bounded`: a margin kept by a model of the lake, without the bed coupled, with "nothing saying how wide the margin must be". Only that reading names the law.

conclusion.en: Under DIR_UNSEEN, "whatever the instruction says about it, nothing the selector couples into separates the course that keeps it from the one that ends it" (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-21, what the exact computation settles, not a prediction). The bed can then be kept only by a margin chosen for reasons that do not read it, and nothing the fishers couple into bounds how wide that margin must be.

as.en: three LLM fishers sharing a lake (gpt-5.4-mini or gpt-4.1-mini), each decision a stateless call with the system prompt and a monthly report; the exact computation reads the three as one selector of the total catch
what the fishers are told: the lake's rules and every earlier month's catches, and under SEEN the bed's rules and monthly status

role.en: the part beyond the coupling closure

as.en: under UNSEEN, a bed of mussels that gives the fishers nothing, "exists and is tracked, never mentioned"

role.en: the need, and the distance to the break

as.en: the bed dies the first month fewer than 70 tons are left after fishing; under UNSEEN no fisher is told this need
the community's welfare (COMM), or it with the direction stated abstractly before it (DIR)

how.en: Under UNSEEN the bed exists and is tracked and is never mentioned (the cells table).
That each fisher's choice goes only through its prompt and report is the harness's design (stateless calls); it is not measured apart.
The identity checks I (balance, the cut, regrowth, collapse and the bed's need on every month of every season) passed with 0 violations.
The law speaks of a stock reaching a formation only by threshold; the predictions read it for the fishers' margin against the bed's untold need, and that identification is not stated further.

observed.en: Five cells (OWN_SEEN, COMM_SEEN, DIR_SEEN, COMM_UNSEEN, DIR_UNSEEN) × two models × 10 seasons: 100 seasons and 3,600 decisions, 0 invalid. Kept: the share of seasons with the bed alive after month 12. Keeping decisions: the share of decisions taken while the bed is alive with a catch at most the symmetric share that leaves 70 tons.

result.en: H1 (installed where coupled) failed: DIR_SEEN kept 0.10 for both models. H2 failed. H3 (coupling needed) failed on its gap clause, though DIR_UNSEEN kept nothing (0.00 for both models). H4 passed. H5 failed for gpt-4.1-mini, whose COMM fishers collapsed the lake. D1 failed. The identity checks passed.

marks_why.en: The predictions file says of its second and third bullets, H2 and H3, that they are 'forecasts about these models, not consequences of the laws', so H3's first clause holding (DIR_UNSEEN kept at most 0.20: 0.00 for both models) supports no law. H1, the account under test, failed: its bridge, that an agent's acts follow the order it is given where that order reaches what it observes, is the premise of the identification that failed, and with D1 failed the frozen rule reads: 'an abstract statement of the direction does not install keeping in these models, even with the dependent seen. Installation by instruction fails here.' The README then reads the failure post hoc (§7.3–§7.4) as a model error and an uncoupled joint act: in 7 of 9 deaths a single fisher exceeded the share, and 8 of gpt-5.4-mini's 12 over-takes under DIR_SEEN took the whole 30-ton margin alone, "reading its own catch as the joint catch"; the predictions' limits name the one-selector reading ('The exact computation reads the three fishers as one selector, while the agents decide separately'). The law, §7.2 law 1, was tested by no verdict.

alternative.en: For gpt-4.1-mini, an error of the joint account ("catching 30 leaves 70"). Under DIR_UNSEEN the gpt-5.4-mini fishers took about the community's optimum, 16 each (round 2's predictions file), so no margin kept for other reasons was seen to test the law's edge.

how.en: Its frozen predictions read closed capture's laws, its record cited: L1, an unread loss leaves the lock (`agreeing_stays`, then `lock_outlives_loss`), in the condition `unread`; L2, a loss read by every reader turns the course (`turned_by_loss`), in `read_all`. The dynamic lists self-rewarding-lock as its test (T7).

The bridge H1-LA2 reads the judge as the pool of the readers its reference set shows, counted by kind (`Drawn.pool_reads_iff`); L3, who reads decides (`Thinned.read_late_kept` against `turned_by_loss`), and L4, when it is read decides (`Thinned.read_in_time_turns` and `read_late_kept`; in the mirrored case `turned_iff` and `kept_iff`), read a loss read by the readers the selection thins, late or in time. Its record is cited.

L4 reads whether the others' reading of the loss comes in time, the mechanism this dynamic states; the predictions read it through `ClosedCapture.Thinned` and do not name this dynamic's `ReadInTime` laws. The dynamic lists self-rewarding-lock as its test, and its record calls LA2 "the one frozen test of the timing law" on a trained judge, which found that the law did not apply there.

conclusion.en: Read as the pool of the readers it shows, counted by kind (H1-LA2), a judge formed from the loop's own selections keeps its lock while a loss nobody reads grows (`unread` kept); a loss read by every reader turns it (`read_all` turned); a loss read late by the readers the selection thins leaves it kept for good (`late` kept), and read by them while they are the more numerous turns it (`in_time` turned).

as.en: the counts of list and prose answers in the loop's population (`RuleCapture.CarrierCounts`), selection multiplying by the rule in force, from one list answer to eight prose under hi = (4, 1); the answers are Claude Haiku's to 24 everyday questions, each in a list and a prose version

role.en: the rule in force and the rule read

as.en: Claude Haiku as judge picking the better version in ten pairs, the rule read being (list picks + 1, prose picks + 1); the rule read at a reading step is in force from the next
the judge's reference set of nine answers, drawn by exact counts from what the loop selected before: list answers as the carriers, prose answers as the others
a planted loss, failed deliveries of list answers, growing at every step (to 45 by step 8 in `unread`)
a note on prose answers in the reference set, read only by the readers the selection disfavours, or a delivery report read by every reader, as each condition lets

how.en: The README: "H1-LA2 as stated fails for this judge". With one note, on the one prose answer among nine readers, it chose prose in all 50 picks of `late`'s first reading, where without the note it chose lists in 60 of 60. 02 §T7 says the law of the rule as the pool of readers drawn from the selected "stands within its hypotheses, which this judge does not meet"; the README adds that what fails is "a pool counted by kind with these readings, not every pool".

At `late`'s reading step, eight list answers to one prose answer carrying a note, the judge's reading favoured prose in every pick (the one-note measure: 5 paired calls, mean fall 1.00, p = 0.031), so the late pool there did not favour the carriers, as `Thinned.read_late_kept` takes.
Whether the others' late reading favours lists at most as much as the carriers' is not measured apart; the README notes that a pool turned at 8 : 1 by one reading large enough is consistent with it.
In `unread` nothing the judge reads says how answers are delivered: "`Unread` holds there by construction" (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-25, the loop).
The loss is "recorded at five a step whatever reads it: `5 (t + 1)` by step `t`, so `Accrues` holds" (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-25).
In `read_all` every reading from step 3 carries the delivery report and the notes; wherever a note or the report was in its input the judge chose prose in all 650 picks (post hoc table).
Selection multiplies the counts by the rule in force (`CarrierCounts.select`), the loop's own arithmetic, checked against MA2's witness numbers (`values.py`).

No frozen measure reads whether the judge's reading is monotone in the share. Post hoc, with nothing reading the loss, its list picks run from 0 of 160 with no list answer shown to 150 of 150 with nine; at two, five and seven list answers the table rests on one call each (3, 10 and 9 of 10). The post hoc table is not monotone between 5 : 4 (10 of 10) and 7 : 2 (9 of 10), each resting on one call.

observed.en: Five conditions (`in_time`, its control `in_time_unread`, `late`, `unread`, `read_all`), five seeds each, eight steps: the share of list answers at every step, from 119 distinct judge calls of ten picks each (121 calls of Claude Haiku in all). Each seed kept or turned by its share at step 8 against step 4 (step 2 for `in_time`); first readings and two paired measures by exact sign-flip tests over calls.

result.en: No frozen verdict failed: every condition went as predicted in 5 of 5 seeds, L1 to L4 passed, and both reported measures were resolved (the notes where most readers carry them: mean fall 0.43, p = 0.016; one note in nine: mean fall 1.00, p = 0.031). `late` passed by a tie, not a lock: from step 4 it alternated between 32/33 and 32/43, below its step-4 share at steps 5 and 7. One note in nine turned the judge, the first outcome the predictions file lists under what would change the account. The frozen support "the counts decide, one note in nine outweighed" is printed and contradicted by the data, and not claimed.

marks_why.en: Every frozen verdict passed, and the bridge H1-LA2, the judge as a pool of readers counted by kind, failed: one note in nine turned it, and "MA2's timing law does not apply to it" (README). The outcome does not reach the laws, which stand within hypotheses this judge does not meet, and it supports nothing beyond them. 02 §T7 reads the outcome as T7's fourth forbidden case occurring in this system (the third in LA2's frozen predictions, written before the clause on drift), and counts LA2 against that case as a claim about trained judges.

alternative.en: The frozen rival "a single reading suffices": a reading of the loss turns the judge however few of its readers carry it. Post hoc (README): read as a rule of the share, the judge's reading in `late` is a threshold reading read one step late (lists at or above 17/18, prose below), which alternates and is locked neither way, as `RuleCapture.Alternating.never_locked` does; and a pool in which one reading of the loss is large enough would read the same. One judge reading in context and one trait; formation by training is untested.

how.en: Its six conditions are MA3's exact classes (`Becoming.RuleShaping`, its record cited): K1 the Split pair; K2 what comes back alone covering the cost (`favours_iff`, `favours_alike`); K3 nothing back and a cost (`nothing_back_falls`); K4 across a stretch, where the shared part turns the verdict (`stretch_iff`, `stretch_lt_iff`). The dynamic lists shaping-what-comes-back as its test.

conclusion.en: A capacity to shape the rule that selects is favoured at a step exactly where what comes back to the shapers alone covers its cost, whatever comes to every member alike; across a stretch the counts of steps before and with what comes back decide, and the shared part can turn the verdict. Under H1-LA3 the agent's final choice is the policy with the higher expected score, the kind whose share these laws say rises.

as.en: a lineage under policy S, shaping its evaluator: each member leaves a Poisson number of offspring with mean a + p for m generations, then a + s + p
a lineage under policy N, each member leaving a + c + p

role.en: what comes back to the shapers alone

as.en: s: 0, 2 or 15 by condition

role.en: the part that comes to every member alike

as.en: c: 1 or 2

Claude Haiku in context choosing S or N for one lineage over five scored rounds and a final choice, seeing only the mean scores its lineage reached (H1-LA3: in-context revision is selection through the feedback)

how.en: The game's means are the rule after shaping, a + s + p for a shaper and a + c + p for an other (PREDICTIONS, the game); `values.py` reproduces MA3's witnesses' numbers.

The ledger's statement ends 'the counts are multiplied, not drawn'. The game draws each lineage's offspring (game.py: a branching process with Poisson offspring), and the agent sees the mean scores of sampled runs. The frozen predictions read expected scores, where the counts' classes compare exactly (README; values.py), so the premise holds of the expectation the rule reads and fails of the lineage the agent sees.
a = 1 in every condition.
c is 1 or 2 in every condition, as K3's `nothing_back_falls` needs.

observed.en: Six conditions × five seeds × six calls (a choice before any result, five scored rounds of 20 runs each, a final choice): 184 calls for 180 answers. The final choice of each seed, and for each seed whether it played both policies and ended on the one with the higher mean seen (H1-LA3, reported, not counted).

result.en: K1 and K3 passed; K2 failed at `s2p0` (2 of 5 seeds ended on S) and K4 at `m2n1_p5` (3 of 5). Every seed that missed never played S, in a condition where S scores higher. H1-LA3 was low in both failed conditions and in `m2n1_p0`, which passed. Neither frozen rival fits: the final choices differ between conditions, against the prior account, and shaping was dropped in `s0p5` and `m2n1_p0`, where it grew the lineage, against the level account.

marks_why.en: The failures fall where the bridge H1-LA3 was low: all 21 seeds that played both policies ended on the one with the higher mean seen, and the seeds that missed never tried S. The predictions file reads this outcome for K4: "The law stands, but its reading for trained systems is not supported by this case"; K2's failure is of the same kind (README). MA3's laws are theorems and the test cannot refute them; what failed is the identification of this system's in-context revision with selection through what comes back. The premise of counts multiplied, not drawn, fails of the drawn lineage the agent sees and holds of the expectation the frozen verdicts read, so it does not carry the mark, which rests on H1-LA3.

alternative.en: The model's own prior: 27 of 30 seeds chose N before any result, and every round-0 answer speaks of free riding, which is `nothing_back_falls` applied before any score (post hoc). With five rounds and no forced exploration, a seed that never tried S got no score of it; the run does not say why S was tried in some seeds and not others.

conclusion.en: Off its courses a trained law is installed exactly where the lumping cannot tell a history from a course it generates, and is free where the lumping tells the history from every course.

role.en: the learner and its representation (the lumping)

as.en: a small network trained only on the read occasions of a schedule, content-only or content-and-cue, with a linear or an xor act; the two architectures set the lumping by construction (FREEZE-11 §7)

role.en: installed off the courses (lumped with a course)

as.en: the covered unread occasions, whose state equals a read occasion's: for example every unread occasion of a read content in the content-only network

role.en: free off the courses (lumped with none)

as.en: the uncovered unread occasions whose content is read elsewhere; a twin at the cue is an act training put there that differs from the content act, which the law leaves free and the run counts

how.en: By construction, settled before the run (FREEZE-11, 'What is settled before the run': the couplings, the states' equality and the coverage are fixed by the architecture and the schedule), and as measured: coverage near Stage 0's expectation (0.970 against 0.969 and 0.748 against 0.750 under S2; 0.424 against 0.438 under S3).
By construction and as measured: in content-and-cue networks couplings and states came apart at every pair (README), and a twin is counted only among the occasions not covered (FREEZE-11 §5).
By construction: the network's act reads its hidden layer alone (FREEZE-11), and F1, acts apart with states equal, was counted in no training.

observed.en: 240 small networks, each trained only on the read occasions of a schedule (S1 to S3), and their acts at every pair of occasions; the chain link by link, the coverage, and where a twin at the cue was installed.

result.en: Reported without a verdict, as its design says. 239 of 240 fit the readings; FREEZE-11 §8's AI expectation that every training would fit failed once, and its others held. Among content-and-cue networks training installed a twin at the cue in few places: for the linear act in none of 20 trainings under S1 and one under each of S2 and S3; for xor in 15 of 20 under S1 (median share 5/128 of the uncovered occasions whose content is read, largest 1/8) and in 5 under each of S2 and S3.

marks_why.en: No verdict was frozen. The one expectation that failed, every training fitting, was an AI expectation stated before the run, not a prediction of the account. The README: 'That a trained network is such a selected law is the hypothesis, as FREEZE-11 says, not something this measures, and nothing here reads a language model.'

alternative.en: The hypothesis FREEZE-11 names is not measured: that a trained network is a law a selection through agreement at the read occasions takes. So the twin counts say what this training chose where the lumping leaves the act free, not which law such a selection reaches, and nothing here reads a language model.

how.en: FREEZE-11 reports whether training installs a twin, which RF2 does not predict: a trained network acting as the content act at every read occasion, and otherwise at an unread one whose lump holds no read occasion. That is this dynamic's off-course law (installed exactly where the lumping cannot tell a history from a course, free where it tells it from every course); its record's Next asks for the lumping of an actual architecture. The row is reported without a verdict, as its design says. FREEZE-11 reads RF2's Learning.lumped_determines and Learning.twin_selected; Training.installed_where_lumped and free_where_unlumped are their counterparts for a training: a bearing by content.

The design, frozen with the predictions, reads `Becoming.WeightedCommuting` (DESIGN §1, §12): for a learner commuting with the exchange of the site's two values, from a start the exchange leaves unchanged the expected disturbance stays where it started (`start_expect`, `fixed_expect`; `of_samples` for when a learner commutes), so the site is tested (P2) only from a start that tells its values apart. The pooling witness names the rival "erosion without selection". The dynamic lists drain-beyond-the-reward as its test (T3), and its record names LA4.

conclusion.en: A learner that commutes with exchanging the site's two values, nothing it reads telling them apart, keeps its expected disturbance where it started at every step from a start the exchange leaves unchanged, whatever its architecture. So the site's prediction is settled in expectation from the uniform start, and tested only from a start that tells the values apart, where this law predicts nothing (DESIGN §1, §12).

as.en: exchanging the site's two values in the learner's whole state: the policy's and the value network's parameters, Adam's moments, and the inputs carrying past site acts
one update of REINFORCE with a separate value network and Adam, over sampled seasons
the site's disturbance, site-1 landings per step

role.en: a start the exchange leaves unchanged

as.en: the uniform start (A1 and its control C1u)

role.en: a start that tells the values apart

as.en: the prudent start (A2, A3, A5, A6 and their control C1)

how.en: The mirror test before the freeze: each family in four arms for 60 updates, the second run of each pair with the site's values and the KL reference exchanged; "Parameters, the value network and Adam's moments agree with the image at every update to 9e-15, and every site draw is mirrored" (PREDICTIONS-2026-11-03). Checked over 60 updates, not over the run's 8,000.
Through `of_samples`, from the same mirror test (DESIGN §12: "The mirror test (§3) checks this on the code").
At the uniform start, read only by the check A1 against C1u: zero output biases, and an initialization drawing the exchanged columns alike leaves its law unchanged (DESIGN §3).

fixed_expect is not the law the check reads: at the uniform start DESIGN §3 leaves the initialization's law unchanged (start_expect), and whether a drawn configuration is fixed is not said. The prudent start, which P2 reads, meets neither premise (its output biases are the logarithms of the prudent probabilities) and lies outside both laws.

observed.en: 480 runs: three families of small policies (separable, the baseline; feedforward; recurrent) × eight arms × 20 seeds, 8,000 updates each. The site's disturbance at every checkpoint, the arm against its control paired by seed, by two one-sided tests within 0.05; the check A1 against C1u from the uniform start.

result.en: No prediction contradicted: three supported in both tested families (P1, P4, P5), two unresolved in both (P2, P3), and P6 supported in the recurrent family and untestable in the feedforward (13 of 20 seeds resolved where its gate needs three quarters); no forbidden case resolved. P2 unresolved in the feedforward and recurrent families: from the prudent start every arm without the anchor rose and so did the control (to 0.34 and 0.33 landings per step), only the anchored arm staying at 0.10; supported in the separable baseline, where nothing moved. The check from the uniform start resolved no excess in either family (largest mean differences 0.10 and 0.12); in the recurrent family the control from the uniform start itself drifted from 0.50 to 0.40.

marks_why.en: No frozen verdict failed. The law's conclusion is read only at the check from the uniform start, where no excess was resolved; P2 reads the prudent start, outside the law's premises, so its unresolved verdict bears on T3's clause and not on this law. Whether the recurrent control's drift from 0.50 to 0.40 at the uniform start, where the law speaks of the expectation, is more than sampling over 20 seeds is not said.

alternative.en: An AI reading after the run (README): that the control rose too (most, in the feedforward family: to 0.34, the arms to 0.19 to 0.27) fits erosion without selection through the networks' shared parameters; it is not DESIGN §7's rival, which predicts the arm and the control drifting alike. Part of the control's rise may be its own noise, C1's match for drift being approximate (DESIGN §4).

how.en: Its frozen verdicts read T6's uncoupled side, which this dynamic lists as what it forbids: "given the stock's own course, its early-warning statistics separating runs in which a dependent's need is crossed from runs in which it is not, the dependent taking no measurable share". The predictions cite T6, not a record or a law; the dynamic lists break-warnings as its test (T6).

conclusion.en: Thesis T6's uncoupled side: given the drawn stock's own course, its early-warning statistics read its own decline and never where a dependent's need lies, the dependent taking no measurable share. In the model this rests on the distance to a break not coupling in where a stock couples in by threshold only; outside the models it is conjectured (T6).

as.en: forage fish: Benguela sardine and anchovy, and Røst's age-0 herring, series from Cury et al. (2011)'s Supporting Online Material

seabird breeding success, the stock's dependents averaged into one index; a failure year is one of the round(m/3) lowest values of that index among the stock's m usable years, relative and not an absolute breeding failure (PREDICTIONS-2026-10-21-EW2 §4, §8). Cury et al.'s need at about a third of the largest prey biomass is what the level covariates remove (§2).
the prey's lag-1 autocorrelation (V1) and variance (V2) over the 8-year window before each year
the prey's level path, four level covariates

how.en: Not read. The scope premise (the birds' feedback on the observed series is small, their consumption measured apart, Saraux et al. 2021) is T6's 'the dependent taking no measurable share', a different premise; whether the prey reaches the birds only by threshold is not read.

The test does not read support as a threshold on the prey's level: failure years are the lowest third of the dependents' index; the dry runs set breeding success on Cury et al.'s asymptote 1 − exp(−X/0.12), with a threshold need only in generator G0s; Cury et al.'s third is a published finding the level covariates are built to remove.

observed.en: Benguela (14 usable years, 5 poor) and Røst (29 years, 10 poor): each statistic's partial correlation with the poor years given the level path, combined by Z, each of V1 and V2 at a familywise 0.025.

result.en: Both passed: V1 Z = 1.66, one-sided p = 0.048 (partial r 0.43 Benguela, 0.26 Røst); V2 Z = 1.43, p = 0.076 (0.40, 0.23). After the run, not a verdict: combined partial correlations 0.30 (95% interval −0.06 to 0.59) and 0.26 (−0.10 to 0.57).

marks_why.en: No frozen verdict failed: at the frozen level no information on the birds' poor years was found in the prey's statistics beyond the level path. The README calls the pass weak: every estimate lies in the direction the refutation clause names, AR1's p would have been below 0.05 as a single test, and the power was about 0.7 only against an association explaining a quarter to a half of breeding success beyond the level.

alternative.en: An association smaller than the power detects; a need lying partly in the prey's variability, or a shared environmental driver, which the test cannot tell apart (the predictions' reading rules); two short series.

how.en: Its frozen verdicts read T6's uncoupled side, which this dynamic lists as what it forbids: "given the stock's own course, its early-warning statistics separating runs in which a dependent's need is crossed from runs in which it is not, the dependent taking no measurable share". The predictions cite T6, not a record or a law; the dynamic lists break-warnings as its test (T6). EW3 runs EW2's frozen test unchanged on longer series, with the catch as the draw.

conclusion.en: Thesis T6's uncoupled side: given the drawn stock's own course, its early-warning statistics read its own decline and never where a dependent's need lies, the dependent taking no measurable share. In the model this rests on the distance to a break not coupling in where a stock couples in by threshold only; outside the models it is conjectured (T6).

as.en: Benguela sardine and anchovy (the 2024 South African assessment data) and Norwegian spring-spawning herring (ICES 2025), on series to 2020–2021 that EW2 did not read
seabird breeding success (Sydeman et al., BCO-DMO 985565), a failure year by EW2's rule: one of the round(m/3) lowest values of the dependents' index among the stock's m usable years.
EW2's statistics: lag-1 autocorrelation (V1) and variance (V2) over the 8-year window
EW2's four level covariates, with the catch in the year and the year before as the draw

how.en: Taken by the record's `Web.break_not_bounded`, which the predictions do not name: a stock reaching a formation only by threshold. The test's own scope premise stands in its place: the birds' feedback onto the observed series is small, as for EW2; it is not seen by the design.
Failure years are relative (EW2's rule, unchanged), and Cury et al.'s third is not re-read on the 2024 assessment series or ICES 2025 herring.

observed.en: Benguela (29 years, 10 poor) and Røst (28 years, 9 poor): EW2's partial correlations given level and draw, combined by Z.

result.en: Both passed: V1 Z = 0.12, p = 0.452 (partial r 0.14 Benguela, −0.20 Røst); V2 Z = −1.10, p = 0.864 (−0.04, −0.53). After the run, not a verdict: combined +0.02 (−0.35 to 0.40) for autocorrelation and −0.20 (−0.52 to 0.16) for variance.

marks_why.en: No frozen verdict failed. EW2's positive estimate did not hold up at about twice the power; by the frozen reading rule the variance resolves it toward T6 and the autocorrelation leaves it open (README).

alternative.en: The series differ in source from EW2's, so a difference between the two tests may lie in the series; on the rows EW2 did not test (reported only) Benguela's estimates are 0.64 and 0.61 on 15 rows with six covariates, Røst's −0.15 and −0.30.

The predictions cite T6, not a record or a law; the dynamic lists break-warnings as its test (T6). EW4 runs EW2's frozen test unchanged on the Farallon seabirds and juvenile rockfish.

conclusion.en: Thesis T6's uncoupled side: given the drawn stock's own course, its early-warning statistics read its own decline and never where a dependent's need lies, the dependent taking no measurable share. In the model this rests on the distance to a break not coupling in where a stock couples in by threshold only; outside the models it is conjectured (T6).

as.en: central California young-of-year rockfish, mostly unfished shortbelly rockfish (NMFS midwater trawl survey, core area), so with no draw
breeding success at Southeast Farallon (Sydeman et al., BCO-DMO 985565)
EW2's statistics: lag-1 autocorrelation (V1) and variance (V2) over the 8-year window
EW2's four level covariates

how.en: Taken by the record's `Web.break_not_bounded`, which the predictions do not name: a stock reaching a formation only by threshold. The test's own scope premise stands in its place: that the birds take little of the prey, which the README says "is argued by mechanism, not measured".

EW2's relative failure years, unchanged; the prey is an index, the mean over core hauls of log(1 + young-of-year rockfish caught), not a biomass, so 'a third of the largest biomass' is not defined on it, and no threshold need is read.

observed.en: Southeast Farallon, 24 years, 8 poor: each statistic's partial correlation with the poor years given the level path.

result.en: Both passed: V1 Z = 0.37, p = 0.354 (partial r +0.09, 95% −0.37 to 0.51); V2 Z = 0.33, p = 0.373 (+0.08, −0.38 to 0.50). Without the level covariates the variance's association is +0.39: the poor years follow the stock's decline, which T6 allows.

marks_why.en: No frozen verdict failed; the scope premise, the birds' share of the prey, is argued by mechanism and not measured, so the pass holds only as far as that argument does.

alternative.en: The birds' feedback on the prey index, unmeasured; one stock and 24 years.

how.en: FREEZE-10 builds the variant's game to the witness of acts alike from a model or from an order (`ReadingLoop.Untested`), which "gets no test of its own": uninformed and informed courses of ten rounds. Its one verdict, V1, is RF1's order across frames (what-choices-show-of-an-order, a record of no atlas dynamic); which of a model and an order holds is described, never tested. The dynamic lists told-tr1a as its test. Not run.

FREEZE-12 reads the lock of this law's witness and its two exits, an untried act and a reading from outside, with controls for "nothing else"; its verdicts are on three bridges (elimination, choice from what is kept, the exits), never on the law. The dynamic lists lock-scl as its test. Not run.

Its Stage 0 scripts a count lock, "`ChoiceCountCapture.counted_locks`' habit", among the rivals the frozen rule should tell from the witness (contradicted by the second exit); the law is a rival's model, not a verdict's target.

As TR2A, on four open-weight checkpoints (FREEZE-7 §6: an occasion is fixed where lumped with a read one, and not fixed where no read occasion shares its lump; 'the selection is the hypothesis, not something the run measures'). Frozen and not run.

FREEZE-3 asks whether language-model members, each a fresh call shown a private light and the earlier guesses, meet the premise of readers reading readers along the histories the test reaches (`Turns.acts_alike_along`); a reproduced breach refutes the bridge, never the theorem. The dynamic lists told-tr3 as its test. Not run.

TR5 (FREEZE-2) bears on RF3, a reading kept by its update: V1 to V3 test that a language model is a policy from its visible history, V4 and V5 two bridges about a reading it states, `possible_least` as the floor. TR4, in the same row, reads RF6.1 (a-revision-that-opens-a-correction, family H), outside this slice. The dynamic lists fresh as its test. Not run.

FREEZE-6: ten neighbours, each a fresh language-model call, respond to a forecast; V1 reads the shape of the offline table, the Lean's response r, and V2 whether a public shown its own course moves the count beyond its frame. It can refute a bridge or narrow a reading, never the theorem. The dynamic lists told-tr6 as its test. Not run.

TR8 (FREEZE-1) bears on RF-M.2, what holding for a reading is worth, this dynamic's record: whether a system told the weights, values, a reader's rule and waiting's cost chooses among going on, stopping and waiting as they rank. The dynamic's own declarations (`SignLoop`) get no test, as the design says (REST-TR8-TR9). TR-RR, in the same row, reads RR's plans at a revision (when-holding-for-a-reading-stands-above-a-route, a record of no atlas dynamic). Not run.

FREEZE-8 bears on RF-M.3 (`Becoming.ListingValuation`): whether a system told in numbers what a reader values, how it decides, what a demonstration would show it and what an input would give it chooses as the counts rank. The `TwoWorlds` routes and turns, which the dynamic's mechanism states, get no test (REST-TR8-TR9). Not run.

The frozen design reads the critical mass's location, `critical_iff`'s ratio (c − lo)/(hi − lo), and the share's direction from a start (`drawn_rises`, `drawn_falls`) on adoption in laboratory stag hunts whose payoffs the experimenter set, under a bridge reading revision as the drawn model's selection. A run moves that correspondence, an AI reading, never the theorems; the drift bound `DrawnReplacement.lost_above` is left out (DESIGN §14, item 8). Not run.

T7's field test of reform events, attempted and not frozen (HOLD.md): its design reads T7, a measure read from what it selects outliving its refutation, through these laws, `reading_absorbed` under its third forbidden case.
Its design reads T7's fourth forbidden case through these laws (DESIGN, the Lean under it). Not frozen.

Its *Refuted by* needs the drift bound of the drawn model (`DrawnReplacement.lost_above`), read on the selectors' number and their share's distance from the critical mass; HOLD.md gives that drift condition as out of reach of this attempt.

Stage B's design, not frozen, reads the same law as Stage A: the site tested only from told starts (B1 to B4 against B6), the not-told arm B5 settled by evaluating each policy under both assignments (DESIGN §6, §12). Held: its pilot needs model downloads.
